hero.title: Bring your mods and shaders to Horizon
hero.lead: Convert Iris / OptiFine shader packs right here in your browser, and Fabric mods with the free desktop app for Windows, Linux and Mac. The translator rewrites them for Horizon, the Rust rewrite of Minecraft Java.

mod.notice.title: Experimental: don't expect a finished mod.
mod.notice.body: The mod converter is a helper, not a one-click port. It does a lot of the work for you, but most mods come out only partly working: anything built on Minecraft features Horizon doesn't have yet is switched off and listed in PORTING.md for you to finish. Try it on a popular mod to see what it does.
mod.download.title: Horizon Translator for Windows, Linux and Mac
mod.download.desc: Mods are converted by a free desktop app, so everything runs on your own PC and nothing is uploaded. It has the same menu as this site and converts shader packs too.
mod.download.small: Windows 10/11, 64-bit Linux or macOS · about 45 MB · Java is included, nothing else to install
mod.steps.title: How to use it
mod.steps.1:
Windows: run HorizonTranslator-Setup.exe. The installer isn't code-signed, so Windows may show "Windows protected your PC": click More info → Run anyway. Only do this with the file from this site or the project's GitHub Releases page. If Defender calls it a trojan, see how to check the file below.
Linux: unpack it (tar -xzf HorizonTranslator-linux-x64.tar.gz) and run HorizonTranslator/bin/HorizonTranslator. install-menu-entry.sh in that folder adds it to your app menu.
Mac: open the .dmg (Apple Silicon for M1 and newer) and drag Horizon Translator into Applications. It isn't signed by Apple, so the first time open System Settings → Privacy & Security and press Open Anyway.
mod.steps.2: Open Horizon Translator, pick the Mods tab and drop in a Fabric mod .jar.
mod.steps.3: Press Convert mod. The result is saved in Documents/Horizon Translator.
mod.steps.4: If the mod converted fully (rare), you get <modid>.hnmod and the app adds it to Horizon: press Build on the launcher's Mods page. Otherwise read PORTING.md for what's left, then build it with horizon-launcher native-build <folder>/mixins/<modid> --trust-native-code. Only build mods you trust: native mods have full access to your computer.
mod.steps.hint: The app only decompiles mods whose licence allows it (MIT, Apache, GPL, LGPL, MPL, OSL and similar). All Rights Reserved mods are only converted for their author ("I made this mod").
verify.summary: Windows Defender says it's a trojan?
verify.p1: Some versions of Microsoft Defender flag the installer as Trojan:Win32/Wacatac.B!ml. The !ml means a machine-learning model guessed, not that known malware was found. It often guesses this for new installers that aren't code-signed and haven't been downloaded much yet. On VirusTotal, Microsoft was the only one of about 70 antivirus engines to flag the 1.0.0 installer; the others found nothing.
verify.p2: Don't take our word for it. You can check the file yourself without trusting this website:
verify.1: Get the official fingerprint from GitHub. GitHub calculates a SHA-256 hash of every file attached to a release and shows it next to the file on the Releases page. This website can't change that number.
verify.1.live: For the latest release ({0}) GitHub reports: {1}
verify.2:
Hash the file you downloaded. Open PowerShell in your Downloads folder and run 
Get-FileHash .\HorizonTranslator-Setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256
(or certutil -hashfile HorizonTranslator-Setup.exe SHA256 in Command Prompt). If it matches GitHub's hash, your file is exactly the one that was published.
verify.3: Scan it with about 70 antivirus engines. Upload the file to VirusTotal or search for the hash there (results for the latest release). Check how many engines flag it and what names they use.
verify.4: Read the code. All of the app's source code is on GitHub (the app itself is in desktop/src), along with the script that builds the installer (scripts/build-desktop.sh), so anyone can review it or build it themselves.
verify.hint: Only trust a hash you got from GitHub itself. If your file's hash doesn't match, delete it and download it again from the Releases page.

make.download.title: Make your own Horizon mod, no coding needed
make.download.desc: The desktop app's Make a mod tab builds Horizon mods from a form: a HUD box with your coordinates or FPS, chat commands, keys, a zoom key, welcome and reminder messages. Press Make mod and you get a ready .hnmod, plus the mod's Rust code if you want to go further. Kit mods use only the parts of Horizon kept stable for mods, so they keep working when Horizon updates.
make.download.small: Free · the app tells you when a new version is out · everything runs on your PC
make.steps.title: In five steps
make.steps.1: Install the app and open the Make a mod tab.
make.steps.2: Pick an example under Start from, or start blank, and give your mod a name.
make.steps.3: Tick what it does and fill in the boxes. Text can show {x}, {facing}, {fps} and more.
make.steps.4: Press Make mod. It's added to Horizon for you.
make.steps.5: In the Horizon launcher's Mods page, press Build under "Native build of Horizon", then play that build.

how.title: How it works
how.mods.title: Mods: Fabric → Horizon native mod
how.mods.1: Licence check. Reads fabric.mod.json and any licence file. Open licences pass; All Rights Reserved is refused.
how.mods.2: Decompile. Turns the jar back into Java with Vineflower. The Java stays on your PC and is deleted straight away.
how.mods.3: Map the mixins. Each @Inject, @Redirect, @ModifyArg… is matched to the Horizon function that does the same job, using a mapping table and Horizon's own source.
how.mods.4: Translate Java to Rust. Config, keys, HUD and tick code, maths, JSON, regex, streams and more become Rust that calls Horizon.
how.mods.5: Write a bundle. A horizon-mixin.toml bundle you build into the game with the Horizon launcher, plus PORTING.md listing anything left to do.
how.shaders.title: Shaders: Iris/OptiFine → Horizon pack
how.shaders.1: Load it like the game does. Runs Horizon's real shader loader (GLSL → naga → SPIR-V) offline, for every dimension, and lists each program it would skip.
how.shaders.2: Fix what fails. Tries about 20 rewrite rules on the GLSL (3D textures, compute passes, out-arguments, buffer formats…). A rule is kept only if more programs load and nothing that loaded breaks.
how.shaders.3: Fix how it draws. Passes that work around differences in how Horizon renders: normals, matrices, missing uniforms, cleared buffers, noise textures, skies.
how.shaders.4: Write the pack. A -horizon.zip for Horizon's shaderpacks folder, with a report of every change.
how.more: The full technical description is in the project's README on GitHub.
faq.title: FAQ
faq.1.q: How do I install a converted shader pack?
faq.1.a: Put the downloaded …-horizon.zip in %APPDATA%\horizon\shaderpacks (Windows) or ~/.local/share/horizon/shaderpacks, then pick it in Options → Horizon Settings → Shader Packs.
faq.2.q: How do I install a converted mod?
faq.2.a: Unzip the bundle. Horizon native mods are compiled into the game, so build it with the Horizon launcher: horizon-launcher native-build <bundle>/mixins/<modid> --trust-native-code. Only do that for code you trust: a native mod runs with full access to your computer. Read PORTING.md first.
faq.3.q: Will every feature of my mod work?
faq.3.a: Probably not. The mod converter is meant to help you port a mod, not do it 100% for you. Code that only uses plain Java converts well. Code that reaches deep into Minecraft (custom screens, entity renderers, resource packs) often has no Horizon equivalent yet. Those parts are switched off and listed in PORTING.md, so the mod still loads.
faq.4.a: Your files never leave your computer. Shader packs are converted inside your browser (WebAssembly) and mods by the desktop app on your PC, so nothing is uploaded and there's no server that could keep anything. Decompiled Java is deleted as soon as a conversion ends.
faq.5.q: Something went wrong. How do I report it?
faq.5.a: Open an issue on GitHub or ask on Discord, or press Report a problem under a result to start one with the details filled in. Say which mod or shader pack (with a download link), what you expected, and paste the converter log. Don't attach mods or packs you aren't allowed to share.
faq.6.a: No. It's a community tool and isn't made by the Horizon, Fabric, Iris or OptiFine teams, or by Mojang or Microsoft.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.unofficial: This is an unofficial translation. The official terms of use are in English.
terms.intro: Horizon Translator is a free community tool that converts Fabric mods and Iris/OptiFine shader packs so they can run in Horizon. It is this website and the Horizon Translator app for Windows (together, "the tool"). By converting a file, downloading the app, or using a converted file, you agree to these terms. If you don't agree, don't use the tool.
terms.1.title: 1. Only convert what you're allowed to
terms.1.1: Only convert a mod or shader pack if you made it, or if its licence or its author allows you to modify it.
terms.1.2: The mod converter checks a mod's licence and refuses mods that are All Rights Reserved, "no derivatives", or have no clear licence. That check reads what the file says about itself and can be wrong. Making sure you have the right to convert a file is your responsibility, not the tool's.
terms.1.3: The app's "I made this mod" option is only for a mod's own author. Using it for someone else's mod breaks these terms and may break the law.
terms.1.4: Don't use the tool to get around a licence, copy someone else's work, or pass it off as your own.
terms.2.title: 2. Converted files are for your own use
terms.2.1: Converted files are a modified version of someone's work. Use them yourself, and only share them if the original licence allows sharing modified copies. Most shader pack licences don't.
terms.2.2: Credit the original authors as their licence asks. Conditions found by the licence check are listed in the converted mod's PORTING.md.
terms.3.title: 3. No warranty
terms.3.1: The website, the app and the converters are provided "as is", without any warranty. Converted mods and shader packs may not work fully, or at all, and the mod converter in particular is experimental.
terms.3.2: Converted mods are native code compiled into your game. Read what you build and only build mods you trust. Keep backups of your worlds and files.
terms.3.3: The Windows app isn't code-signed. Only download it from this site or the project's GitHub Releases page.
terms.3.4: To the extent the law allows, the people who make the tool aren't liable for any loss or damage from using it or the files it produces.
terms.4.title: 4. Your files and privacy
terms.4.1: Your files are never uploaded. Shader packs are converted inside your browser and mods inside the app on your own computer. Decompiled code is deleted as soon as a conversion ends.
terms.4.2: The site doesn't use accounts, cookies or tracking. It is hosted on GitHub Pages, and loads two small libraries from public CDNs (jsDelivr and cdnjs), which see your visit like any website would.
terms.4.3: The app works offline. It only goes online when you click a link, which opens in your browser.
terms.4.4: Donations are voluntary gifts. They don't buy anything, can't be refunded, and don't create any obligation.
terms.5.title: 5. Acceptable use
terms.5.1: Don't use the tool to make or spread malware, or to break the law.
terms.6.title: 6. Copyright complaints and takedowns
terms.6.body: If you believe the tool, the project's source code, or anything it hosts infringes your rights, open an issue on GitHub with: what work is yours, what you believe infringes it, and how to reach you. Complaints are taken seriously and handled as quickly as possible. The tool never receives or stores the files people convert, so there is usually nothing stored to remove, but the converters' behaviour can be changed (for example, to refuse a specific mod or pack).
terms.7.title: 7. Not official
terms.7.body: The site is a community project. It isn't made by, endorsed by, or affiliated with Mojang, Microsoft, the Horizon project, Fabric, Iris, OptiFine, or the authors of any mod or shader pack. "Minecraft" is a trademark of Mojang AB.
terms.8.title: 8. Changes
terms.8.body: These terms may change. The date at the top shows the latest version. Using the site after a change means you accept it.
